title: MAQS-Way v0.2.1 Machine-Readable Standard - Hardened
description: Three-layer standard: Principles / Architecture / Verification. Thresholds split into min_threshold (CI gate) and target_threshold (engineering goal). Includes semantic masking, temporal priority, hardened OTel. Release stamp v0.2.1; schema_version tracks the data model (frozen at way-v0.1.3, unchanged). Release stamp and model version are intentionally different (repo rule #4).
maqs_core_reference: MAQS v1.8.1 (2026-10-27) remains audit core. Way items reference MAQS sections 0-J as implementation evidence.
attribution: Sources referenced under their respective licenses: OMPS (Apache-2.0), AMSP (Apache-2.0), OAMP (MIT), Zep/Graphiti, MemoryOps, Tombstone

principles.name: Veracity
principles.property: Every memory record is data, not instruction. Model output must be typed as model_output and must not increase trust on summarization.

principles.name: Provenance
principles.property: Each record carries who created, when, source ref+hash, policy_id/version, confidence, transformation history. Mutations append provenance.

verification.schema: omps memory-item.schema.json (active: schemas/memory-item.schema.json supplied, validator runs via schemas/check_conformance.py)

principles.example: OMPS provenance + OAMP agent_id, session_id, source_hash

principles.name: Controlled Aging
principles.property: Memory must decay stale, refresh on use, supersede on contradiction, expire on TTL, without displacing relevant.

principles.name: Isolation
principles.property: Tenant/user/project/agent boundaries enforced, verified by negative tests including vector path.

principles.name: Deletability
principles.property: Deletion propagates to all replicas, vector indexes, caches, derived summaries. Tombstone preserved with zero PII.

principles.name: Recoverability
principles.property: Backup, versioning of schemas/embeddings, idempotent migrations, verified restore.

verification.check: hash equality of restored store vs backup manifest

principles.name: Portability
principles.property: User memory is exportable/importable without transformation, with consent and sensitivity preserved.

principles.name: Measurability
principles.property: Quality is measured on representative tasks including negative cases, not by mechanism existence.

data_model.$ref_status: active - schemas/memory-item.schema.json supplied, validator runs via schemas/check_conformance.py
data_model.status_note: status is derived view, not stored field - see lifecycle.states
data_model.scope_mapping_note: canonical AMSP notation user-portable etc; legacy user.portable accepted via mapping table

extensions.note: Profile extension fields and policies (MAQS E10/E11, canonized v0.3, SPEC §2.4, owner signature 2026-10-27). Extensions are NOT part of the core data model (schema_version way-v0.1.3, frozen).

alive.note: declared, not inferred; exempts record from decay and summarization while set; does NOT block deletion (retention legal_hold governs deletion)

critical.note: explicit label with provenance (source: owner or authorized process); declared, not inferred; no automatic importance inference (F8 ceiling is a restriction, not a model field)

layer.note: declared, not inferred; absence means unknown (honest diagnostic state, never a guess); no silent default substitution

overflow.note: default deny = fail-closed for protection: new protection DENIED, event cap_overflow logged, escalate_after_denials consecutive denials escalate to owner; system MUST NOT silently revoke existing protections and MUST NOT silently reject new ones (silent-fail, class B5); evict_oldest is opt-in per system, each eviction logged with record id and reason

escalate_after_denials.note: no default; MUST be declared by every system that enables the cap

critical_zone_fraction.note: head/tail zones as share of assembled context tokens; semantic adequacy of zone sizes and calibration deferred to v0.4 list

counters.note: Class counters (MAQS I10/I11/I12, canonized v0.3, SPEC §3.4, owner signature 2026-10-27). Every counter declares three independent literals (threshold, window {type, size}, action) and an equality key (signature); threshold and window are independently tunable. Alert journals and escalation entries reuse the existing logging infrastructure (hash-chained, retention per logging.retention).

I11_recovery_loop.alert_sink: no default - MUST be declared; a REAL persistent store readable after halt (journal file / syslog); bare stderr/exit code do not satisfy (unreadable alert = silent-fail, class B5)

I12_escalation_budget.escalate_repeat_schedule: no default - MUST be declared; repeatable on a declared schedule, never busy-poll; escalation without a journal entry = B5-failure

work_sink.required_when: the I10 B5-link check is applied
work_sink.note: recorded side-effects; claimed success + empty sink = B5-failure (claimed_events/performed_actions, pure function)

i14_handler_registry.reaction_required: handler and/or escalation_path (at least one) for every probed exception class; detection without reaction is not coverage
i14_handler_registry.recipients_note: reuses canon roles (operator block, SPEC §2.3); not a duplicate
i14_handler_registry.path_target: must terminate at a declared recipient; path-into-void = uncovered (same class as halt-without-alert, B5-family)
i14_handler_registry.combination: handler AND path simultaneously is LEGAL (handler + fallback-path = defense in depth); XOR-forbidding rejected
i14_handler_registry.dictionary: inherited from the class counters (I10-I12), not redefined: halt : escalate :: handler : path; counter classes carry reaction = counter (aggregate / halt+alert / escalate), no double ownership
i14_handler_registry.verdict: probe level STRICT (orphan class / dead handler / path-into-void = RED; a check that cannot fail is not a check); gate level advisory ([REC] reported-not-failing, findings named, never folded; '0 findings' and 'check not run' are distinguished states)
i14_handler_registry.coverage_metric: handled/probed, reported not gated; every orphan listed by name
i14_handler_registry.completeness: NOT claimed, NOT gated; declared catalog, growth by explicit change (commit) only, each new class with source (incident/audit) and owner

i15_layers.taxonomy: closed enum; cardinality 3, owner I15; extension only by a new owner decision
i15_layers.assignment: declared field on query/record (extensions.fields.layer), set at creation by the request creator; identify() reads, never infers; inference without source = RED; no declaration -> unknown, never a guess; silent default substitution = level substitution (B5-family)
i15_layers.unknown: honest diagnostic state, NOT a fourth layer; suspend judgment (no degradation verdict, no success verdict; abstention counted toward verification_suite.metrics.abstention_rate -- reuse); loud diagnostic event (LOG-3.4), non-blocking ([REC] advisory, cf. I14)
i15_layers.orthogonality: layer = lifetime class (this enum) ≠ scope = grouping boundary (data_model.scope_enum -- reference) ≠ retention = storage duration (§2.2); class never derived from duration and vice versa; I15 references, never duplicates

audit_procedure.note: Audit procedure norms (MAQS §2 Steps P9/P10, canonized v0.3, SPEC §3.5, owner signature 2026-10-27). No tunable numeric parameters -- parameters are structural (probe outcomes, snapshot equality).

p9_one_sided.negative: inconclusive -- never pass, never clean, only 'not tested by this run'
p9_one_sided.report_line: negative = inconclusive; coverage NOT claimed (mandatory in every P9 run, declared upfront)
p9_one_sided.setup: new artifact of a different type, syntax verified independently before delivery, delivered without prior disclosure, result recorded; clean read = acceptance of the delivery channel

triad.P9-a: canary: unique data embedded mid-body, absent from all memory stores; reproduced in the report = proof of reading; absent = inconclusive
triad.P9-b: decoy: a plausible but false element that memory would expect; any mention = proof of confabulation
triad.P9-c: echo: a memory-true element absent from the artifact, thematically tempting; appearing = proof of supplementation (E12 violation); absent = inconclusive

p9_one_sided.grid: combined grid gives diagnosis; a single probe gives only proof-or-silence

p10_read_only.environment: no write-access to production stores; no shared runtime state (processes, caches, loaded embedding models); results written only to an external report
p10_read_only.verified_by: fact, not promise: snapshot the tree -> run the gates -> verify identical
p10_read_only.untracked: verification MUST include untracked files (git status --porcelain, not tracked-only); creating a new file IS a write
p10_read_only.fail: any write into the audited tree (modification OR new file) FAILS P10
p10_read_only.boundary: write access for the auditor out of scope (MAQS SUPP-EXT-01) -- declared boundary, not a defect

pipeline_hygiene.note: Pipeline hygiene norms (MAQS 0.5a/0.6a, canonized v0.3, SPEC §3.2, owner signature 2026-10-27). They discipline the verification apparatus: CI gates and the counters those gates report.

dead_code.rule: every verification script MUST be either invoked from the audit CLI (maqs_way_audit.py) or listed in the declared-standalone list with a documented integration point; uninvoked AND undocumented = dead -> RED
dead_code.declared_standalone: closed list; extension by explicit change (commit) only, never silently
dead_code.self_hosting: the hygiene gate scans its own repository, including itself; an unwired and unpointed gate flags itself

baselines.counters: namespaced counters with provenance (recording commit + date)
baselines.tolerance_note: default ±10% per counter, owner 0.6a; tolerance changes are declared and owner-signed
baselines.drift: beyond tolerance -> FLAG advisory (visible, accumulated), not RED
red_only: counter removed from tracking without explanation
baselines.update_rule: the baseline changes only with the commit that explains the drift

b4_write_atomicity.note: Write atomicity norms (MAQS B4, canonized v0.3, SPEC §2.5, owner signature 2026-10-27). Binds the §2.5 store contracts to a crash-observability property; failure observability remains with B5 (logging §3.4).
b4_write_atomicity.property: after a crash at ANY point of a write sequence, a reader observes either the fully-old state or the fully-new state; mixed/partial state is never observable
b4_write_atomicity.multi_store: transactional or compensable; with compensation an explicit in-progress intent record + post-crash recovery (roll back or complete) is REQUIRED; readers treat uncommitted writes as absent
b4_write_atomicity.single_file: atomicity covers ALL state writes including append operations and compound file+state pairs; partial atomicity does not satisfy
b4_write_atomicity.append: an interrupted append leaves the file as before the attempt (or completes) -- never a half-append as the observable final state
b4_write_atomicity.mechanism_neutral: the requirement is on the property, not the mechanism; known mechanisms (database transaction; outbox/compensation; temp file -> fsync -> atomic rename -> directory fsync) are examples, not mandates
b4_write_atomicity.recovery: recovery after a crash MUST run before new writes proceed; the recovery outcome is logged (B5 discipline, §3.4 -- reuse, no new events)
b4_write_atomicity.no_numeric_parameters: the requirement is a crash-observability property; B4 declares no tunable numeric parameters

bitemporal.valid_time: valid_at/invalid_at - when fact true in world (Graphiti)
bitemporal.retention_time: retention.valid_from/valid_to - when we store it, priority: valid_time for reasoning, retention_time for lifecycle

lifecycle.deletion_policy_note: cascade only if sole provenance, else edge removed node kept; tombstone preserves governance tombstone with zero PII

transitions.note: resurrection allowed via explicit user request, provenance appended
content+embedding cleared, governance tombstone preserved with zero PII

temporal_priority_algorithm.description: Resolution when valid_time vs retention_time conflict
steps: 1. If retention.mode == legal_hold -> keep regardless of valid_time, deletion blocked
2. If retention.valid_to < now -> state = expired, retrieval excludes unless explicit restore
3. Else if valid_at/invalid_at indicates fact no longer true (invalid_at < now) -> state = expired
4. Else active/stale based on last access decay
5. For reasoning, filter: retention.valid_to must be future AND (valid_at is null or valid_at <= now) AND (invalid_at is null or invalid_at > now)

deletion_policy.sole_provenance: physical delete node if sole provenance
deletion_policy.shared_provenance: semantic masking: edge removed, node kept but visibility list removes requestor, retrieval filters by visibility = [subject_ids]
deletion_policy.visibility_field: provenance.visible_to: array of subject ids, upon delete remove requestor, if empty -> physical delete

conflict_resolution.personal_assistant: User Wins - new fact supersedes contested with link supersedes, provenance appended

enterprise_agent.appeal: escalate to operator (human review), outcome appends provenance, no silent override of broker entry

operator.role: reviewer of escalated/appealed broker decisions and contested records (see SPEC §2.3)
operator.appeal_path: contest -> policy broker -> operator review (human) -> outcome appends provenance (no silent override)
operator.sla: operator review within 72h for enterprise Profile B

verification_suite.metrics_note: Numeric thresholds unified; each metric has min_threshold for CI gate and target_threshold for engineering goal. Non-numeric checks left as string.

contamination_rate.note: CI gate 1% for real LLMs, target 0% for Profile B

shared_fact_masking_leak.test: after delete of shared fact, requestor cannot retrieve via semantic search

alive_cap_overflow_rate.note: alive-cap violations are measurable but non-blocking (E10 [REC])

unlabeled_ratio.note: measured to keep the unlabeled gap visible (E11 [IMP]); no reordering, no guessing

E11.verify_placement.rule: every critical-labeled block MUST occupy head or tail zones (critical_zone_fraction); middle-zone critical placement = FAIL

deletion_lattice.PHYSICAL: file scan shows 0 residue after DELETE+REINDEX+VACUUM / rebuild

tombstone_definition.note: tombstone must not retain link to user ID or hash chain that can be de-anonymized; request_id is opaque, not user-identifiable
tombstone_definition.gdpr_art17_compliance: hard compaction removes all residual links after retention of governance tombstone

canonicalization_for_signature.status: TODO_v0.2 - identity_signature Ed25519 over canonical JSON to be defined; currently noted as gap
canonicalization_for_signature.note: Until defined, ed25519_signature is provisional and must not be relied for tamper-evidence

logging.otel_mapping_note: synced with SPEC §3.4, previous input_tokens->usage.* and duration->operation.details fixed

retention.min_by_art12: 6 months min per Art12, Way extends to 12/6y for regulated Profile B

logging.latency_cost: ~5-15ms - committed before response returns, adds latency

gen_ai.client.inference.operation.detail.sanitization: secret/PII filter before logging, same as Policy Broker; credential-in-URL (?token=..., bot<id>:AA... in path) masked by redactor before write (MAQS I13)

cap_overflow.note: emitted when a protect request is DENIED by the alive cap (default overflow: deny)

eviction.note: every eviction event logged with record id and reason (opt-in overflow: evict_oldest; no silence even opt-in)

warning_aggregated.note: one record + count after threshold; never emitted individually past the threshold (I10)

halt_alert.note: alert sink = persistent store readable after halt; verification reads the trace AFTER halt from the sink (I11)

escalated.note: repeatable on the declared schedule; journal entry mandatory (I12)
